version.changelog: fix(v1.6.0): watchdog 12-day silent failure due to path encoding bug. Uses 8.3 short path for non-ASCII repo paths.

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed OpenClaw UI patch that modifies local Control UI files and adds a browser-side model picker enhancement, with no evidence of external exfiltration or deceptive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The browser script uses localStorage/sessionStorage, a mutation observer, a one-second heartbeat, and same-origin fetch('./') polling with possible reloads; these are disclosed and tied to keeping the UI enhancement working.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a PowerShell script that auto-detects the OpenClaw Control UI directory, backs up index.html, injects one script tag, copies one versioned asset, and removes only matching old pcl-model-picker assets.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill describes installation, verification, repair, and uninstall commands without hidden role changes, prompt overrides, or instructions to bypass user intent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The injected script and asset persist in the local OpenClaw package until removed or overwritten by upgrade, but the artifact includes an uninstall path and does not include the optional scheduled-task watchdog referenced in history docs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to improve the OpenClaw model picker, and the inspected PowerShell and JavaScript implement that UI enhancement, including hiding the account row, resizing, diagnostics, and update detection.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to patch your local OpenClaw Control UI. Review the PowerShell command before running it, expect a local index.html script-tag injection plus an asset copy, and be aware that open tabs may periodically same-origin check for updates and reload. Use the documented -Remove command to uninstall.
llm.findings:
[RA1] expected: The self-update/watchdog references describe same-origin browser update checks and an optional GitHub-only repair watchdog; the ClawHub artifact inspected does not include scheduled-task persistence or self-modification of the skill package.
[LP1] expected: The network behavior is a disclosed same-origin fetch of the app shell for update detection, with no third-party host or telemetry found in the packaged JavaScript.
[P2] expected: The matched bytes/strings are a UTF-8 BOM in multilingual files and an HTML marker used for the injected script tag; I found no hidden agent instructions or prompt-injection directives.
[AE4] expected: Mixed Unicode content is explained by multilingual documentation and Chinese PowerShell comments/messages, not obfuscation or credential handling.
[SDI-1] expected: Automatic same-origin polling and page reload are broader than a static layout tweak, but they are explicitly disclosed and implemented to avoid downgrades and avoid interrupting active typing.
[SDI-2] expected: The reload mechanism is purpose-aligned with keeping already-open OpenClaw tabs on the patched asset; no remote code execution or external update source was found.
[SQP-2] expected: Reload can occur without an inline prompt, but the documentation discloses this behavior and the code delays while an input, textarea, or contenteditable element is focused.
[SQP-1] expected: The skill description can match common model-picker complaints, but the artifact frames this as an install/repair/uninstall skill and provides explicit shell commands rather than silent automatic installation.
[SQP-3] expected: Language-related findings come from multilingual documentation, Chinese script text, and an English-authoritative license clause; these do not create a security concern for installation behavior.
